answer: An attester must stake 40% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. Because the canyon stake is held until the knoll settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the zephyr audit lists each exposure. A farm running 103 keys as a result burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. That is 4 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
